required_contracts_note: The two fixed_contract_p99_stable_h1_wrk2_* contracts are the wrk2 CO-free latency (p99_stable) family (heavy aggregate + light single-read). Matched conditions to the wrk throughput contracts (128 conns, 4 threads, 60s/120s window, h1, loopback) so they are comparative-eligible on the same allowed_pairs. Isolation is by contract_id (as with v1/v2/single_read), reinforced by a -runtime-wrk2 workload_profile_key suffix that run-comparative.sh derives for runtime-wrk2 contracts: wrk2 latency data never aggregates with the wrk throughput family.

Pure-JDBC (Agroal + PreparedStatement, NO Hibernate/ORM) + native-epoll transport. Comparison-eligible within-tier H1 (community, loopback-h1). AXIS CAVEAT: differs from quarkus-hibernate on TWO axes at once — relational data-access (pure-JDBC vs Hibernate ORM) and Netty transport (native epoll vs JDK NIO); vs exeris-community the persistence layer is matched (both no-ORM) so the pair isolates runtime/transport efficiency. Reports must state these axes, not frame it as a bare quarkus number.

COMPATIBILITY-mode target: the same Spring MVC + JPA app hosted on the Exeris ingress (ExerisCompatDispatcher, ADR-011) instead of Tomcat. Request-path endpoints only (the compat request-scope bug is fixed; saga is NOT eligible). PURE-vs-COMPAT is a mandatory separation axis: this is compat, never blend with pure-mode rows (native Exeris / Tomcat Spring / Quarkus) without the explicit compat caveat. CONFIDENTIALITY: excluded from the public docs path (CLAUDE.md); measurements are Community + Compatibility + H1, internal-only publication. Comparison-eligible within-tier H1 for the spring-hibernate__spring-on-exeris pair, which isolates the Exeris compat-ingress cost vs native Tomcat for one identical Spring app.

PURE-mode target: the same Spring + JPA application as spring-hibernate and spring-on-exeris, hosted on Exeris with the NATIVE web layer (@ExerisRoute + ExerisRequestHandler, no ExerisCompatDispatcher, no Spring MVC on the request path). Third arm of the Spring hosting comparison. Note the two senses of 'pure' on this axis: spring-hibernate is pure because it never touches Exeris (Tomcat + Spring MVC), this target is pure because it bypasses Exeris's COMPATIBILITY layer while still being hosted by Exeris. Both are on the pure side, and neither may be blended with the compat row without the caveat. Eligible for the FULL contract family, heavy and light, since exeris-spring-runtime #50 (ExerisRouteRegistry.resolve now strips the query string before lookup); before that fix the light single-read contracts were unroutable here and the target carried an eligible_contracts restriction. BUILD REQUIREMENT: light eligibility depends on the runtime build, not on this target's source — a jar built against a pre-#50 runtime 404s on /api/v1/user?id=1 while still passing every heavy contract. Verified 2026-08-02 against exeris-spring-runtime-web 0.5.0-SNAPSHOT with kernel 0.10.2: light and heavy both 200 and byte-identical to the other two arms. FOOTPRINT: RSS IS comparable with spring-on-exeris. An earlier note here claimed otherwise on the assumption that the missing exeris-spring-runtime-flow dependency left whole subsystems unstarted; that was wrong. Both arms boot the kernel SubsystemOrchestrator with Selector=ALL and initialise all eight subsystems including events and flow — the kernel flow subsystem is not the Spring flow module. The real difference is the Spring-side saga/graph beans: 551 extra loaded classes in the compat arm and 2.59 MB more metaspace (77.34 vs 74.75 MB). Measured locally n=1 after two forced full GCs under identical flags (-Xms256m -Xmx1280m) and identical read-only load: RSS 483 MB compat vs 485 MB pure — the pure arm marginally HIGHER, i.e. the delta is below run-to-run noise and does not run in the direction the old caveat assumed. Campaign RSS must still be reported per arm; what is retired is the claim that the two are incomparable. CONFIDENTIALITY: excluded from the public docs path, as with spring-on-exeris; measurements are Community + H1, internal-only publication.

The SAME exeris-community-app jar (kernel 0.10.1) with the ADR-052 Blackbird JsonMapperCustomizer uber-jar added to the launch classpath — Jackson-3 invokedynamic property accessors replacing the default megamorphic MethodHandle on the response-encode path. Comparison-eligible within-tier H1 ONLY for the exeris-community__exeris-blackbird pair; it is a WITHIN-EXERIS serialization-accessor A/B (both arms identical except Blackbird), NOT a cross-runtime target. Its default arm (exeris-community on 0.10.1) also cross-checks the 0.10.0 aggregate baseline (ADR-052 seam is default byte-identical).

2x2 serialisation-matrix arm 1: exeris-community-app built with -Dexeris.kernel.version=0.10.1 and launched from a version-staged jar, default Jackson-3 MethodHandle accessors. Comparison-eligible ONLY inside the within-exeris matrix pairs; never a cross-runtime number.

2x2 serialisation-matrix arm 2: same staged 0.10.1 jar as exeris-k0101 plus the ADR-052 Blackbird customizer on the launch classpath. A leaf counts only if the bootstrap breadcrumb proves the customizer applied. Within-exeris matrix pairs only.

2x2 serialisation-matrix arm 3: kernel pinned to 0.10.2, default accessors. Its contrast with exeris-k0101 covers the WHOLE v0.10.1..v0.10.2 encode/allocation batch (#241 + #244), not SegmentSink alone — label it that way. Within-exeris matrix pairs only.

2x2 serialisation-matrix arm 4: kernel 0.10.2 plus Blackbird. The arm carrying the accessor-by-encode interaction. Same customizer jar as arm 2 (seam byte-identical across v0.10.1 and v0.10.2). Within-exeris matrix pairs only.

allowed_pairs.axis_note: Both no-ORM: isolates runtime + transport efficiency (exeris native runtime vs Quarkus/Vert.x native-epoll + virtual threads), NOT ORM cost.

Same runtime (Quarkus), differs on data-access (Hibernate ORM vs pure-JDBC) + transport (JDK NIO vs native epoll): quantifies the ORM+transport delta within Quarkus, the decomposition context for exeris-vs-quarkus-tuned.

COMPATIBILITY-COST pair (Pure-vs-Compat axis): the same Spring MVC + JPA app, same iso-2048 heap, hosted on native Tomcat (spring-hibernate, pure) vs the Exeris compatibility ingress (spring-on-exeris, compat). Quantifies the Exeris compat-seam overhead. AXIS CAVEAT: the arms are NOT ingress-only. The compat arm cannot declare a servlet SecurityFilterChain — under spring.main.web-application-type=none its mere presence suppresses ExerisSecurityContextFilter — so the pure arm runs a filter-chain authorization decision per request while the compat arm runs the kernel's context filter instead. That difference is forced by the ingress choice, so it belongs inside the measured seam cost, but the seam number is NOT decomposable into transport-only from this pair alone. AUTH AXIS: both arms serve the benchmark read endpoints (/api/v1/users heavy, /api/v1/user light) unauthenticated — no Authorization header is sent by any driver and the Tomcat arm matches them permitAll — so this pair measures no authentication work. It does NOT measure zero security work: the Tomcat arm still reaches a per-request authorization decision through its filter chain while the compat arm runs the kernel's context filter, and the two are not equivalent. Both arms do at least carry spring-boot-starter-security, which spring-on-exeris-pure does not; state the axis on any three-arm comparison. Equalising it needs matching rules on both sides (SecurityFilterChain vs ExerisHttpSecurity) driven by a token-bearing scenario. Internal-only publication: spring-on-exeris is excluded from the public docs path; never frame as a pure-mode number.

HOSTING-SWAP pair, third arm vs first: one Spring + JPA application served by Tomcat + Spring MVC (spring-hibernate) versus the Exeris native web layer (spring-on-exeris-pure). This is the best case for hosting the application on Exeris, because it bypasses the compatibility seam that spring-hibernate__spring-on-exeris measures. AXIS CAVEAT: the arms differ on more than the socket — ingress, web layer, request-decoding path and serialisation entry point all change together, and the pure arm has no servlet filter chain, so this is a whole-hosting delta and is NOT decomposable into transport cost. Serialisation is held constant deliberately (both encode via the same autoconfigured Jackson ObjectMapper), as is everything below the web layer. Heavy and light contracts both run; responses verified byte-identical across all three arms on 2026-08-02. AUTH AXIS — MUST BE STATED WITH ANY NUMBER FROM THIS PAIR: the measured traffic is unauthenticated (no Authorization header in wrk/wrk2/h2load/k6; both read endpoints are permitAll), but the arms are NOT equal in per-request security work. spring-hibernate carries spring-boot-starter-security and runs a full servlet SecurityFilterChain, which still reaches an authorization decision on every request even when the match is permitAll. spring-on-exeris-pure does not carry Spring Security at all, so it runs NO per-request security code. That difference is a confound inside this pair, not part of the hosting seam, and on the light contract — where per-request fixed cost dominates — it favours the pure arm. Until both arms can declare equivalent rules (Spring SecurityFilterChain vs Exeris ExerisHttpSecurity) and be driven by a token-bearing scenario, treat this the way the pgjdbc fetch-config normalisation is treated, with more weight because it is the security layer. Internal-only publication.

COMPAT-SEAM pair (Pure-vs-Compat axis in its cleanest form): the same application on the SAME host runtime, differing only in whether requests traverse the Exeris compatibility layer (ExerisCompatDispatcher + ExerisSpringMvcBridge + MVC argument resolution) or the native ExerisRequestHandler path. Unlike spring-hibernate__spring-on-exeris, the transport, kernel and carrier are identical on both sides, so the delta attributes to the compat dispatcher rather than to hosting as a whole. FOOTPRINT: RSS, throughput and latency are all comparable across this pair. Both arms boot all eight kernel subsystems (Selector=ALL, events and flow included) — the compat arm's extra exeris-spring-runtime-flow dependency adds Spring beans, not subsystems. Measured difference is 551 classes and 2.59 MB of metaspace, with post-GC RSS 483 MB compat vs 485 MB pure (local n=1, identical flags and read-only load): below noise, and marginally in the opposite direction from what the missing dependency would suggest. Heavy and light contracts both run. AUTH AXIS — MUST BE STATED WITH ANY NUMBER FROM THIS PAIR: the measured traffic is unauthenticated, but the arms differ in per-request security work and the difference is NOT part of the compat seam. spring-on-exeris carries spring-boot-starter-security and, because a servlet SecurityFilterChain is structurally unavailable under spring.main.web-application-type=none, runs the host runtime's ExerisSecurityContextFilter instead (its JwtDecoder bean is present, which is what activates the filter). spring-on-exeris-pure carries no Spring Security at all and runs nothing. So part of any measured seam cost here is 'compat arm has a security filter, pure arm has none' rather than 'the compat dispatcher is slower', and the effect is largest on the light contract. Equalising it needs ExerisHttpSecurity on the pure arm with rules matching the compat arm, plus a token-bearing scenario; until then no seam number from this pair may be reported without this axis stated. BUILD PARITY IS ALSO PART OF THIS AXIS: both arms must be built against the same exeris-spring-runtime and therefore the same kernel — they are currently matched at kernel 0.10.2, raised from 0.9.0 by exeris-spring-runtime #50. Rebuilding one arm without the other reintroduces a kernel-version variable into a measurement whose entire purpose is to isolate the compat dispatcher. Internal-only publication: both arms are excluded from the public docs path.

WITHIN-EXERIS serialization-accessor A/B (NOT cross-runtime): identical exeris-community-app on kernel 0.10.1, differing ONLY in the ADR-052 Blackbird customizer (default Jackson-3 MethodHandle accessors vs invokedynamic). Isolates whether Blackbird cuts the ~20% BeanPropertyWriter.get/invokeExact response-encode CPU measured 2026-07-19. Report as a within-exeris tuning delta, never as an exeris-vs-X number.
2x2 serialisation matrix, ACCESSOR lever at the OLD encode path (arm1 vs arm2). Same staged 0.10.1 jar; only the Blackbird customizer's classpath presence differs. Within-exeris tuning delta only.

2x2 serialisation matrix, ACCESSOR lever at the NEW encode path (arm3 vs arm4). Same staged 0.10.2 jar; only the Blackbird customizer differs. Comparing this delta against exeris-k0101__exeris-k0101-bb gives the interaction. Within-exeris tuning delta only.

2x2 serialisation matrix, ENCODE lever at DEFAULT accessors (arm1 vs arm3). Measures the whole v0.10.1..v0.10.2 encode/allocation batch (#241 response streaming + #244 buffer-release accounting; #242 is inert for GET), NOT SegmentSink in isolation. Label accordingly. Within-exeris version delta only.

2x2 serialisation matrix, ENCODE lever at BLACKBIRD accessors (arm2 vs arm4). The second, independent route to the interaction: (arm4-arm2)-(arm3-arm1) must agree with (arm4-arm3)-(arm2-arm1). Disagreement means one arm is not what it claims to be. Within-exeris version delta only.
